title: Alaska: nonexempt registration and acknowledgement precede the offer
affectedParty: Actual seller or supplier, operator and responsible management team
applicability: Only sales/offers within AS 45.66.070 of a business opportunity not excluded by .220.
requirement: Section .010 requires seller registration at least 30 days before the sale or offer begins. Under .020(c) and 9 AAC 16.010, registration is complete only on receipt of the department acknowledgement. The filed packet includes disclosure, promotion materials, bond, consent and application. Section .080 and 9 AAC 16.020 require purchaser disclosure at least 10 calendar days before the earlier contract signature or receipt of consideration.
exceptions: An established .220 exclusion removes this chapter; independent federal disclosure can still apply. Filing an application does not itself complete registration.
deadline: Registration complete at least 30 days before offer/sale begins; disclosure at least 10 calendar days before the earlier stated commitment event
evidence: Disclosure delivery, signed receipt and earliest commitment calendar

title: Alaska: nonexempt renewal, material changes and bond duration have different clocks
affectedParty: Actual seller or supplier, operator and responsible management team
applicability: A continuing nonexempt seller registered under AS 45.66.010.
requirement: Section .030 requires annual renewal by the acknowledgement anniversary while offers/sales continue; .050 requires a material-change statement within 10 days. 9 AAC 16.060 specifies the adopted change form and hand-delivery or certified-mail methods. 9 AAC 16.030 requires the bond during offers/sales and for three years after the last sale.
exceptions: These are the nonexempt chapter obligations, not filing obligations imposed by the source on every Part 436 franchise. The agency form being dated 2005 is consistent with the express administrative incorporation.
trigger: Continuing offers/sales, material information change or final sale
deadline: Renew by anniversary; material changes within 10 days; bond through three years after last sale
renewal: Annual while the specified activity continues
evidence: Material event, prescribed form and delivery proof

title: Alaska: nonexempt contract rights include cancellation and nonwaiver
affectedParty: Actual seller or supplier, operator and responsible management team
applicability: Only a contract within the nonexempt AS 45.66 business-opportunity chapter.
requirement: Section .090 requires a written contract and specified terms. Section .130 permits cancellation for any reason on written notice within 30 days after signing and separately lists additional cancellation grounds. Under .130(e), refund and termination of buyer financial obligations follow within 15 days after notice; buyer makes supplied items available within five days after refund. Section .170 prohibits and voids buyer waivers of chapter rights or defenses.
exceptions: These are business-opportunity contract rights, not a universal Alaska franchise termination or nonrenewal regime. The established Part 436 exclusion and other .220 exclusions must be tested first.
trigger: Drafting or administering a covered opportunity contract or cancellation
deadline: 30-day ordinary buyer cancellation; 15-day seller refund after notice; five days after refund for buyer item availability

title: Louisiana: a required opportunity bond continues beyond the initial filing
affectedParty: Actual seller or supplier, operator and responsible management team
applicability: Only bonds for business opportunities in RS 51:1821(1)(a), (b) or (c), as limited by 51:1822(G).
requirement: Section 51:1822(H) makes a required bond continuous. A surety may terminate it on 60 days written notice to the assistant secretary and principal; liability continues during that period and for accrued pre-termination liability discovered later. Section (E) requires any new/additional bond before continuing business.
exceptions: This is surety-bond administration, not a 60-day franchise-contract termination rule. It does not apply automatically to every marketing-plan or trademark licence.
trigger: Bond status change, surety termination notice or continued covered business
deadline: 60-day surety notice under the specified bond provision; required new/additional bond before continuing business
renewal: Continuous term, subject to the specified surety process
evidence: Replacement security and continuing-business release record
interpretationLimits: Only the stated statutory branch is reviewed. Other franchise, sector, contract, federal and local law remains separate.

title: Maine: covered opportunity disclosures and registrations have separate update triggers
affectedParty: Actual seller or supplier, operator and responsible management team
applicability: A seller of a covered Title 32 Chapter 69-B business opportunity; apply definition and exclusions first.
requirement: Section 4696 requires updating the disclosure statement as material information changes. Section 4697 makes a registration effective for one year from effectiveness; annual renewal requires a current disclosure statement, required fee and evidence of qualifying security. Failure to renew expires the registration.
exceptions: This is the covered business-opportunity registration track, not a finding that every franchise is included or excluded. The source is current through October 1, 2026 and is not the officially certified annotated text.
trigger: Material disclosure change or anniversary of registration effectiveness
deadline: Material-information update; annual renewal before registration expires
renewal: One year from effectiveness; annual renewal with the specified inputs
evidence: Applicable bond/escrow evidence and renewal receipt

title: Nevada: a covered farm-equipment agreement change also needs good cause
affectedParty: Actual seller or supplier, operator and responsible management team
applicability: Only the farm-equipment dealer agreement and inventory defined in NRS 597.112–597.114.
requirement: Section 597.1143(1) requires good cause for termination, nonrenewal or a substantial change of dealer-agreement terms. Section 597.115(4) separately prohibits those actions because of specified uncontrollable circumstances. Section 597.118 prohibits waiver or modification of the statutory rights, obligations and liabilities.
exceptions: The 180-day notice and 60-day correction provisions in .1143(2)–(3) concern termination/nonrenewal; no general 180-day amendment deadline is inferred. The chapter is not a general service-franchise statute.
trigger: Proposed substantial term change, termination or nonrenewal
deadline: Assess before the action; do not transplant the termination/nonrenewal notice period to every amendment
evidence: Defined inventory and actual dealer agreement
